chapter: Joining Raeburn and work for other leaders
title: His recorded songs: 'Rip Van Winkle' and others
summary: He lists songs recorded by Ella Mae Morse, Bobby Troup, Jo Stafford and Eckstine and what they earned.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I might as well ask it on camera, we were going over the list of the people you had worked for before Raeburn, cleaning up that area of history, and commenting on such.
On the back of one of my albums is a list of the bands I had been with,
Is that the same list there?
Incidentally, the names of the tunes that were recorded by Ella Mae Moss (Morse) there, what are the names?
"Rip Van Winkle".
That made me some money. You're asking which came close to being a hit, I guess that would be it because it was in the movie, I heard about.
What movie?
Something with Jane Withers and in the picture, Jane Withers sang the tune.
Like everything else I find out about my music, someone told me they saw the picture and she sang it.
You didn't get a magnificent check for use in the movies?
I recall no magnificent check, but that particular tune did make me more
money than the others. I had a few records on it.
Three people did "Where You At", Bobby Troup, Dave and Jimmy and Gary Trio.
Right.
That's been bringing in money in dribs and drabs.
"You Were Loved So Well", Jo Stafford did.
That was never released.
I don't remember the tune; have I ever heard the tune?
Probably not.
I'm sure it's not on any of the Raeburn material.
No, I never wrote it for the Raeburn band. I was about to.
"If Love Is Trouble", Eckstine recorded that.
